status_summary: No order amending Executive Order 13526, no cut to original classification authorities and no ODNI-run automated declassification system was found. The closest structural step is Executive Order 14243 (signed 2025-03-20), whose section 3(f) told agency heads to review whether their classification policies lead to over-classification and to report to OMB within 45 days with recommendations; no report or follow-on action was found. Separately, ODNI's Director's Initiatives Group used AI tools to speed record-specific releases (DNI Gabbard's remarks of 2025-06-10), and releases continued under Executive Order 14176 and agency decisions through the CIA's President's Daily Brief release of 2026-09-11. Those releases share the Mandate's goal of more disclosure but not its structural design.

timeline.event: President signs Executive Order 14176 directing release of federal records on the assassinations of John F. Kennedy, Robert F. Kennedy and Martin Luther King Jr., with plans from the DNI and Attorney General due within 15 days (JFK) and 45 days (RFK and MLK); it does not amend Executive Order 13526.

President signs Executive Order 14243 (published 2025-03-25, 90 FR 13681); section 3(f) directs agency heads to review their classified information policies for classification beyond what is needed to protect critical national security interests and to report to OMB within 45 days, cataloguing the policies and recommending whether any be eliminated or modified.

In answers to Senate Intelligence Committee questions, ODNI nominee Aaron Lukas says the Director's Initiatives Group will help develop recommendations to modernize the declassification process (date inferred from the document's file name).

At the AWS Summit in Washington, DNI Gabbard says AI tools helped the Director's Initiatives Group release JFK and Robert F. Kennedy assassination records much faster, and that ODNI is evaluating AI tools that could be bought once for all 18 intelligence community elements; the report describes no plan to automate declassification community-wide.

CIA declassifies 54 documents, about 1,450 pages, on Robert F. Kennedy under Executive Order 14176, bringing its total to more than 200 documents and nearly 5,000 pages; the effort was led by DNI Gabbard with DOJ, FBI and NARA.
Ratcliffe declassifies an internal tradecraft review of the 2016 election intelligence assessment.
CIA releases President's Daily Briefs to mark the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks.

title: Modernize classification and declassification and cut original classification authorities
uncertainties: The finding of no structural reform rests on Federal Register searches (presidential documents mentioning classified national security information since 2025-01-20, and all documents mentioning Executive Order 13526, which returned only agency notices) and web searches that returned mostly Obama-era material; an order or ISOO rule not indexed under those terms could exist. Executive Order 14243 was re-read on 2026-10-18: section 3(f) asks for an over-classification review and a report to OMB within 45 days and does not mention declassification, original classification authorities or Executive Order 13526; the outcome of that review (due about 2025-05-04) was not found. ODNI pages on declassification could not be checked because dni.gov was unreachable, so an ODNI-run declassification initiative published only there cannot be ruled out. The Director's Initiatives Group is described only through a nominee's written answers and a trade report of Gabbard's remarks; the date of the Senate document is inferred from its file name. The Senate Intelligence Committee's FY2027 authorization bill (S. 4615, reported 2026-08-05) would require notice to Congress of certain declassifications under Executive Order 13526 but does not address original classification authorities, over-classification or declassification funding, and it has not been enacted. The earlier record's 2026-06 ODNI COVID-origins release was dropped because it rested on a Wikipedia summary and is record-specific.
